I'm James Cook, a controls engineer. My PhD applied deep and reinforcement
learning to engine modelling and optimization, and I've spent most of my career
on UAV flight controls and drone programs.

## Why I built this

I've spent a long time as a student: a BS, two MS degrees, an MBA and a PhD.
Looking back, the handful of professors who did an amazing job all taught in a
way I was receptive to. I learn best from visuals, and from real-world examples
I can tie back to things I already know.

Most lessons I find offer good visuals or good examples, and often neither. With
help from large language models, I can now build the lessons I wish I'd had: an
encyclopedia of topics I find interesting, including machine learning, deep
learning, reinforcement learning, automotive engineering, finance, math and
controls. Hence the name. I use it to refresh my memory and to prepare for
quantitative job interviews.

## How the lessons work

Each lesson follows the same pattern: why the idea matters, the theory with one
diagram, a real problem it solves, an interactive graphic you can drag or step
through, the minimal math, a worked example, code you can run in your browser,
and practice questions.

Lessons point to each other only where one truly builds on another, so you can
start anywhere. The [lesson map](map.qmd) shows how they connect.

Everything here is open source. If something is wrong or unclear, open an issue
on [GitHub](https://github.com/jamesc91/jimcyclopedia), or find me on
[LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/james-robert-cook). If you've found this
page, I hope you enjoy it and find it helpful.

::: {.vl-start}
**To get started, pick a lesson from the list on the left.** On a phone, tap
the book icon just below the site name to open the list.
:::
